clue.text: A 19 animal, by virtue of being a horse that went the wrong way?

parts.note: qua is Latin-derived English for 'in the capacity of, by virtue of being'

indicators.note: going the wrong way means the pair of pieces before it is read backwards

parts.note: gee-gee, GG, is nursery and racing slang for a horse

explanation.surface: A riddle about an animal that died out, being a horse whose line went the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: '19' points to the answer at 19 across, gone for good: the animal died out. 'that went the wrong way' reads like the animal's fate but turns the pair 'a horse' back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: The quagga was a South African zebra relative hunted to extinction in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Nimble third man is a help in the field

parts.note: quick means nimble
Harry Lime is the title figure of the film The Third Man

explanation.surface: A nimble fielder at third man helps out on the cricket field.
explanation.walkthrough: Third man is a cricket fielding position, but here it is Harry Lime from the film The Third Man. The field is farmland.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmers spread burnt lime on fields to reduce soil acidity.

clue.text: Fond, as Gloucester said, of the looking-glass?

definitions.text: as Gloucester said, of the looking-glass?

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean duke speaks of being fond of his mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard, Duke of Gloucester, in Richard III says he is not made 'to court an amorous looking-glass'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fond means loving, and Gloucester's phrase pairs the loving adjective with a mirror.

clue.text: Advance and inherit the earth

explanation.surface: Move forward and come into the world's soil.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a literal reading: to gain ground is to get land.
explanation.definitionFit: To make progress is to advance; read literally, it is acquiring land.

clue.text: Silly idiot, leaving No 10, becomes a writer of love stories

indicators.note: the letters of silly idiot become something new once rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letter pool
taken as written, part of the letter pool
10 is read as the letters I and O, which leave the mix

explanation.surface: A foolish fellow quits Downing Street and turns romantic novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No 10' looks like Downing Street but is the letters I and O. Take them from SILLYIDIOT and rearrange the rest, SILLYIDT, under 'becomes'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a tale of pastoral happiness or romance, and its author is so called.

clue.text: A service for the courses in Worcester or Derby

definitions.text: A service for the courses in Worcester or Derby

parts.words: A service for the courses in Worcester or Derby
parts.note: a set of crockery for meals, as made by the Worcester or Royal Crown Derby porcelain firms, not a race meeting

explanation.surface: A service for the racecourses at Worcester or the Derby.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is a famous horse race and Worcester has a racecourse, but here they are English porcelain makers.
explanation.definitionFit: Plates and dishes for an evening meal sold as a matching collection.

clue.text: Drunk in America, fresh and juicy

explanation.surface: Drunk in the US, and fresh and juicy.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for a heavy drinker; also luxuriant and succulent, of plants.

clue.text: Said jokingly, a number of things taken into the body

definitions.text: number of things taken into the body

indicators.note: said means the phrase for jokingly is spoken and its sound kept

parts.note: in jest means jokingly

explanation.surface: Someone says, in fun, a number of things swallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingesta is a plural noun for matter swallowed as food.

clue.text: Herb the bank blower known to Oberon

definitions.text: the bank blower known to Oberon

explanation.surface: A herb that grows on a bank, known to the fairy king.
explanation.walkthrough: Oberon in A Midsummer Night's Dream says 'I know a bank where the wild thyme blows'.
explanation.definitionFit: A culinary herb; Oberon's speech names it blowing (blooming) on a bank.

clue.text: A seaweed derivative often' duplicated

parts.note: a jelly made from seaweed whose name is often said twice over with a hyphen

explanation.surface: A substance from seaweed is frequently copied.
explanation.walkthrough: The jelly is also called agar-agar.
explanation.definitionFit: A gelatinous substance from red algae used in laboratories and cooking.

clue.text: Evening out in the club with gin cocktail

parts.note: an iron is a kind of golf club

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of gin are shaken up

explanation.surface: A night out at the club with a gin cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evening out' reads as a night on the town but means smoothing creases; 'cocktail' turns GIN into ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing clothes flattens and smooths them, making the fabric level.

clue.text: Small numbers, for example, always form a bunch in the garden

parts.note: nos is the short form of numbers, hence small
eg is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example
ay (aye) is an old word for always or ever

explanation.surface: Small numbers always group together, like flowers in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A posy is a small bunch of flowers, as picked from a garden.

clue.text: Grand token exchanged in this elaborate plot

indicators.note: the letters of grand and token are exchanged among themselves into a new order

explanation.surface: A large token is traded inside an intricate scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' suggests a scheme, but it is a garden bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal garden bed laid out in an intricate interlacing pattern of low hedges is so named.

clue.text: Man is one, eight are reported

explanation.surface: Man is one of something, and eight of them are spoken of.
explanation.walkthrough: Man here is the Isle of Man. An ait (eyot) is a river island, and 'eights' said aloud is aits, so eights are islands by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea; aits, sounding like eights, are small river islands.

clue.text: It makes deep sounds — thus states blower

parts.note: so means thus
the USA is the United States
blower is British slang for the telephone

explanation.surface: Something booms out, and a trumpeter declares as much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blower' suggests a wind player but is slang for the telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bass brass instrument that produces low notes.

clue.text: Out but not far from the Strand, we hear

definitions.text: Out but not far from the Strand, we hear

parts.words: Out but not far from the Strand, we hear
parts.note: out at sea yet close to the beach, strand being an old word for a shore rather than the London street

explanation.surface: Someone is away, but not far from the Strand in London, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: The Strand is a famous London street, but a strand is also a beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Waters near the coast, off the beach but close to land, are described this way.

clue.text: New text about dog as a sociable creature

indicators.note: the scrambled word goes about the word for dog
new means the letters of text are made new

parts.note: Rover is a traditional name for a dog

explanation.surface: A fresh text about a dog presenting it as friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' turns TEXT into EXTT, which goes 'about' ROVER.
explanation.definitionFit: An outgoing person who enjoys company.

clue.text: Bear a breadbasket

explanation.surface: A bear and a basket for bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breadbasket' is slang for the belly.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to tolerate it; breadbasket is joke slang for the belly.

clue.text: Darkest, inner section of a plane?

definitions.text: Darkest, inner section of a plane?

parts.words: Darkest, inner section of a plane?
parts.note: the dense dark core of a plane tree's trunk, not a part of an aircraft

explanation.surface: The darkest inner part of an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: The plane is a tree, not an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The dense central wood of a tree trunk, usually darker than the sapwood.

clue.text: Gone for good measure of codex tincture?

indicators.note: a measure of something is a portion of it, so a run of letters is taken from the two words

explanation.surface: A dose of tincture prescribed in an old manuscript has run out.
explanation.definitionFit: A species that has died out completely has vanished for ever.

clue.text: One is hailed and spoken of as a fair carrier

definitions.text: spoken of as a fair carrier

explanation.surface: Someone acclaimed and praised as a fair bearer.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading: 'fair carrier' sounds like fare carrier, a vehicle taking paying passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired car with a meter that picks up passengers in the street.

clue.text: Square set out according to Mosaic Law, presumably

definitions.text: set out according to Mosaic Law, presumably

explanation.surface: A square laid out in line with the Law of Moses.
explanation.walkthrough: Mosaic Law is the Jewish law given to Moses, but here it is the art of mosaic, in which such pieces are set.
explanation.definitionFit: A small square tile of stone or glass, the unit from which a mosaic is laid.

clue.text: Not direct in one's answers, see viva ruined?

indicators.note: ruined means the letters of see viva are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Look how the oral exam was spoiled by dodging questions.
explanation.walkthrough: A viva is an oral university examination.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dodges questions gives roundabout replies.

clue.text: Passage formerly dry on the outside

indicators.note: the word for dry sits on the outside of the word for formerly

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means dry, not drinking alcohol
ex means formerly, as in ex-wife

explanation.surface: A corridor that used to be dry on its exterior.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is an extract of writing, a portion of the words.

clue.text: Pound of pulse?

parts.note: the beat of the heart in the pulse, not a weight of lentils or beans

explanation.surface: A pound of peas or beans.
explanation.walkthrough: Pulse looks like dried beans, and pound like a weight; both are about the heartbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong rhythmic beat, as of the heart.

clue.text: Family works to get something in the pot

parts.note: a house is a family line, as in the House of Windsor
a plant is a factory or works

explanation.surface: The family business goes to pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant grown indoors in a container.

clue.text: Bread and milk — things given to pacify

explanation.surface: Bread and milk handed out to calm someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces of bread soaked in milk; also concessions offered to appease.

clue.text: Press in expedition?

explanation.surface: The press on an expedition.
explanation.definitionFit: To press is to hurry; expedition means speed or haste.

clue.text: Concerning _ clues altered or withdrawn

parts.note: re means concerning, about

indicators.note: the letters of clues are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: About clues being changed or taken back.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit keeps away from society, having retired from it.

clue.text: Beef in first part of next month

indicators.note: the word for beef goes in the word for first part

parts.note: primo is the first part of a piano duet
an ox is a beef animal

explanation.surface: Beef appears in the opening part of next month's menu.
explanation.walkthrough: PRIMO is the musical term for the upper or first part in a duet.
explanation.definitionFit: Old business usage: proximo means of the coming month.

clue.text: Shilling with change — note it could make an American quail!

parts.note: a bob was British slang for a shilling, an old coin worth twelve pence

indicators.note: with change means the letters of with are rearranged

parts.note: E is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: With a shilling and some change, a note could buy an American quail.
explanation.walkthrough: BOB was slang for the shilling, an old British coin worth one twentieth of a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American game bird named for its call.

clue.text: Member has intention to become a celebrity

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
an end is an aim or intention

explanation.surface: A member intends to become famous.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous person is called a living legend.
